Take a short walk around the immediate hotel neighborhood to get your bearings and pick up any essentials from a nearby convenience store.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Rome's Historic Downtown for a relaxed first-evening stroll. Explore Broad Street, admire the Clocktower, and soak in the small-city charm. Browse any open shops or galleries as part of an informal preview of the Downtown Art Walk you'll do more thoroughly later in the trip.

meals.lunch: N/A - in transit / airport snacks

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light since you're arriving in the afternoon. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Average high is ~30°C so stay hydrated. Check if La Quinta offers a free continental breakfast for the following mornings.

day_by_day.morning: Start with the hotel's complimentary breakfast if available, then head out to the Rome, GA Historic Downtown Art Walk. Spend the morning exploring vibrant murals, public art installations, and local galleries scattered throughout downtown. Pick up a free walking map from the Rome Area Council for the Arts or download one online. This is entirely free and a great way to see the city's creative side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring downtown galleries and pop into any free-entry art spaces. Visit the Rome Area History Museum (low admission fee, typically under $5) to understand the local context. Grab lunch and rest during the hottest part of the day (around 1-3 PM) to avoid the ~30°C heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to cool off, then head back downtown for the cooler evening hours. Walk along the Oostanaula River trail near Riverside Park for a scenic and free outdoor experience. End the evening with a casual dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel complimentary breakfast or grab a coffee and pastry at a local café for under $5
meals.lunch: Partridge's Restaurant on Broad Street - classic diner-style meals, budget-friendly at $8-12 per person
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli - casual, affordable sandwiches and comfort food, around $10-14 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Art Walk is self-guided and free. Bring a reusable water bottle and sunscreen given the June heat. Morning hours (before 11 AM) are the most comfortable for outdoor walking.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, drive or rideshare to the Chieftains Museum & Major Ridge Home Tour on Riverside Parkway, just minutes from Chateau Drive. This National Historic Landmark offers a fascinating look at Cherokee history and the story of Major Ridge. Admission is typically around $8-10 per adult - excellent value for the depth of history covered.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend additional time on the museum grounds exploring the outdoor areas and the historic home. Afterward, head to a nearby local eatery for lunch. Visit the Rome Braves stadium area (AdventHealth Stadium) nearby for a look around - if there's a home game, budget tickets can be as low as $6-10 for a fun, affordable afternoon activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to downtown Rome for the Friday evening atmosphere. Check local listings for any free live music or community events on Broad Street, which are common on Friday evenings in summer. Enjoy dinner at a downtown restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local bakery
meals.lunch: Zaxby's or a local fast-casual spot near the museum area - budget $8-10
meals.dinner: Coosa Valley Brewing or a nearby pub with food - enjoy local craft beer and affordable pub fare around $12-15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check the Chieftains Museum website ahead of time for current hours and admission prices. Friday evenings in downtown Rome often have community events - check the Rome, GA events calendar online.

day_by_day.morning: Head out early (before the heat peaks) to Berry College for the Campus Art & Nature Walk. Berry College is one of the largest college campuses in the world by acreage and features stunning Gothic architecture, on-campus art collections, and beautiful natural landscapes. Entry to the campus is free. Walk through the Ford Buildings area and the historic quadrangle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Berry College's scenic trails and natural areas. The campus has deer, wildlife, and peaceful forested paths - bring a picnic lunch to enjoy on the grounds and save money. Visit the on-campus art installations and the college's historic mill area if accessible.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rest and cool down. In the evening, explore a different part of Rome's dining scene. Saturday evenings are lively in downtown Rome - consider visiting the Rome Farmers Market if it runs into evening hours, or browse local shops before dinner.

meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local grocery store (Kroger or Walmart nearby) - sandwiches, fruit, and drinks for under $10 total
meals.dinner: El Ranchero Mexican Restaurant - generous portions, authentic flavors, very budget-friendly at $10-13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is a working college campus - be respectful of students and facilities. Wear sturdy walking shoes for the nature trails. Bring insect repellent for the wooded areas. Start early to avoid peak afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit the Historic Downtown Art Walk with fresh eyes - focus on any galleries or murals you may have missed on Day 2. Many local galleries have rotating exhibits, so there may be new things to see. Visit the Capitoline Wolf statue replica, a famous Rome landmark, and explore the Seven Hills of Rome area for a unique photo opportunity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely afternoon drive or walk to Myrtle Hill Cemetery, a beautiful and historically significant hilltop cemetery with panoramic views of the city - completely free to visit. This is a peaceful, shaded spot that's cooler than open streets. Afterward, visit a local art supply or craft shop to pick up an affordable souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed Sunday evening. Cook a simple meal in the hotel room if you have access to a microwave/mini fridge (pick up groceries from a nearby store) to save on dining costs, or opt for an affordable takeout option.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Rome Pizza & Pasta - casual Italian-American spot with affordable lunch specials around $9-12
meals.dinner: Takeout from a local spot or a simple grocery store meal to keep costs down - budget $6-10

day_by_day.notes: Sunday can be a slower day in Rome, GA - some shops and galleries may have reduced hours. Use this as a relaxed exploration day. Myrtle Hill Cemetery offers great views and is a hidden gem that most visitors overlook.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning walk or jog along the Etowah River Trail or the Rome Riverwalk - a free, scenic path along the river that's beautiful in the early morning before the heat sets in. This is a great way to experience Rome's natural beauty and get some exercise. The trail connects several parks and offers views of the river confluence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rome Area Council for the Arts (RACA) gallery space downtown for any current exhibitions - admission is typically free or by donation. Spend time in any air-conditioned galleries or museums to escape the afternoon heat. Browse local antique shops on Broad Street for unique, affordable finds or souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: For your second-to-last evening, treat yourself to a slightly nicer but still budget-conscious dinner experience. Explore any local food trucks or pop-up dining events that may be happening downtown - Rome has a growing food scene. End the evening with a walk along the river at sunset.

meals.lunch: Broad Street Baking Company - fresh sandwiches, soups, and baked goods at very reasonable prices, around $8-11
meals.dinner: The Forrest on Broad - a local restaurant with a seasonal menu; look for weekday specials to keep costs around $15-18 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Riverwalk is best enjoyed before 10 AM or after 5 PM in June due to heat. Check the RACA website or social media for any special Monday events or gallery openings. This is a good day to do any souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome, GA. After hotel checkout (or storing luggage at the front desk), take one last stroll through Historic Downtown to pick up any last-minute souvenirs, local art prints, or food items. Visit any gallery or mural spot you want to photograph one more time. Stop by a local coffee shop for a farewell breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, make a final visit to a favorite spot from the week - whether that's Berry College, the Chieftains Museum grounds, or simply a peaceful sit by the river. Use this time to reflect on the trip and ensure you have everything packed.
